quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, how does a motorcycle respond to turning and speed changes?

options.text: More slowly than usual.
More quickly than usual.
Normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to the motorcycle. This extra weight makes the motorcycle slower to respond. It takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn.

questions.question: When riding in the rain, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: Ride down the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in tire tracks left by other cars.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery when rain first falls. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. This gives you better grip on the road.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Use your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
Use your mirrors. You only need to look over your shoulder if something seems wrong.
Either use your mirrors or look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check that no other vehicles are in your way. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder toward the lane you want to enter.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you tell them to do?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before the engine starts.
Sit as far back as possible on the bike.
Avoid talking and moving when the motorcycle is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking and moving when the motorcycle is moving.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger not to talk or move unnecessarily while riding. Passengers should only get on after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as they can without getting in your way.

questions.question: When riding in a group, how should motorcyclists travel?

options.text: In a staggered formation.
In single-file formation.
Side-by-side.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is the best way for a group to stay close while keeping enough space between riders. Use single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or leaving highways. Side-by-side riding is dangerous because riders lose their escape routes.

questions.question: When is there less grip available for braking?

options.text: When a motorcycle is leaning.
When a motorcycle is straight up and down.
When a motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a motorcycle is leaning.
questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans during a turn, there is less grip for braking. You can still use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, the center of the lane is safest. Riding near the passing vehicle risks a crash. Riding far from it may make the driver return to your lane too quickly and unsafely.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It links the front and rear brakes together when you apply the rear brake.
It automatically applies the brakes by learning your riding habits.
It connects to the gears and applies the brake when you shift down.

questions.correctAnswerText: It links the front and rear brakes together when you apply the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems. When you press the rear brake pedal, it links both brakes together. Check your owner's manual to learn about your specific motorcycle's brakes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They show traffic laws for that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What is the best clothing for a motorcyclist?

options.text: Feels uncomfortable.
Provides protection in a crash.
Should not stand out to other motorists.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides protection in a crash.
questions.explanation: Good riding clothes protect you if you crash while keeping you comfortable and visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic
Right lane ends
Merge

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols or letters. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that traffic ahead will merge.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on a straight road:

options.text: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You will need to release the rear brake to regain control of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can usually control your motorcycle even with a locked rear wheel, as long as the motorcycle stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Allow you to blend in with traffic.
Provide an escape route.
Encourage others to use your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide an escape route.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should stop other drivers from sharing your lane and give you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to change to red.
The traffic light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you the light will turn red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: To lower your chance of a crash, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Scan your path ahead.
Be ready to act to avoid a hazard.
Turn your headlight off during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your headlight off during the day.
questions.explanation: To prevent a crash, always make sure others can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: When making a normal stop on a motorcycle:

options.text: Only the front brake should be used.
The front and rear brakes should be applied at the same time.
Only the rear brake should be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear brakes should be applied at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, use the front and rear brakes together and shift to a lower gear.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Protects your face, but not your eyes.
Protects your eyes, but not your whole face.
Helps protect your whole face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes, in a crash. A windshield alone does not give enough protection.

questions.question: The rear brake control is usually located:

options.text: On the right handlebar.
On the left handlebar.
Near the left foot.
Near the right foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot.
questions.explanation: The rear brake on a motorcycle is operated with the right foot.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcycle takes:

options.text: Less time than usual to stop and speed up.
The same amount of time to stop and speed up as it usually does.
More time than usual to stop and speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: More time than usual to stop and speed up.
questions.explanation: Extra weight slows down a motorcycle's acceleration and braking. Your motorcycle will respond more slowly to your commands when you have a passenger than when you ride alone.

questions.question: You get the most protection from a helmet if it is all of the following, except:

options.text: U.S. DOT-compliant.
Loose-fitting.
Free of defects.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loose-fitting.
questions.explanation: A helmet gives the best protection when it meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what is true about mirrors?

options.text: The mirrors show everything around you.
The mirrors cannot show your blind spots.
You should only use mirrors when parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: The mirrors cannot show your blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots, just like car mirrors. Always turn your head to look for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What color are service signs?

options.text: Orange with black letters.
Blue with white letters.
Green with white letters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks at an angle, what should you do?

options.text: Use the road shoulder to slow down before crossing.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Ride straight across within your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight across within your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride straight across angled tracks within your lane. Changing your angle could move you into another lane and cause a collision with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: The right
The center
The left

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed from behind or by oncoming traffic. This keeps both you and the other driver safe.

questions.question: When you are about to pass a vehicle on the left, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: The left portion
The center portion
The right portion

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This improves your view ahead and helps other drivers see your intention to pass.

questions.question: What should you do when the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Proceed slowly and carefully.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at a railroad crossing with flashing lights. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to drive faster than a train.

questions.question: If sunlight makes it hard to see your turn signals, what should you do?

options.text: Keep using the mechanical turn signals.
Honk your horn to tell other drivers about your turns.
Use hand signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use hand signals.
questions.explanation: Use hand signals when sunlight makes your turn signals hard to see. It is important to clearly tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: What should you know about taking over-the-counter medication before riding?

options.text: It is usually fine because over-the-counter drugs are not strong.
It is acceptable at all times.
It may hurt your ability to ride and should be done carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may hurt your ability to ride and should be done carefully.
questions.explanation: Many medications, including over-the-counter drugs, can affect your ability to ride safely. Talk to your doctor about how any new medication might affect your riding.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay safe while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Look far ahead of your motorcycle.
Stay away from busy traffic areas.
Ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Always look ahead on the road while riding. Watch for hazards in the distance so you can react to them before you reach them.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: No parking is allowed.
It marks the right edge of the traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: It marks the right edge of the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road shows the right edge of the traffic lane.
